questions.question_text: An organization wants to connect multiple VPCs across different AWS regions for secure and scalable communication, while minimizing costs. Which three options should the architect choose? (Select THREE)
options: A. Use apex records for DNS resolving between VPCs
B. Implement Transit Gateway peering attachments across regions
C. Configure VPC endpoint services using PrivateLink
D. Set up software VPN tunnels between VPCs in the same region
E. Deploy Direct Connect links between VPCs
questions.explanation:
A. Apex records are used for DNS resolving within AWS and not between VPCs across regions, making it inappropriate for this scenario.

B. Transit Gateway peering attachments across regions provide a simpler management of VPC-to-VPC communication than VPC peering, making it an optimal choice for secure and scalable connections across regions.

C. VPC endpoint services using PrivateLink allow direct access to AWS resources from VPCs without exposing the VPC to the internet, which is cost-efficient and secure.

D. Software VPN tunnels between VPCs in the same region are more complex to set up and maintain than Transit Gateway peering attachments across regions, making them less optimal for this scenario.

E. Direct Connect links can be used but they are costly and not necessary if Transit Gateway peering attachments can satisfy the requirements.

questions.question_text: A company has multiple VPCs spread across different AWS regions and wants to enable secure, scalable, and cost-effective communication between them. Which option should the architect recommend for this requirement?
options: A. Use AWS Transit Gateway to connect all VPCs into a single virtual network.
B. Deploy multiple VPC Peering connections between each pair of VPCs.
C. Set up Software VPN tunnels with internet gateways attached to each VPC.
D. Create Direct Connect connections for each VPC and route traffic through them.
questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway is the best choice as it provides simpler management of VPC-to-VPC communication compared to multiple VPC Peering connections, especially with a large number of VPCs. It also allows for central visibility and logging through Flow Logs, which can be published to CloudWatch Logs and Amazon S3. 

Option B (VPC Peering) would become unmanageable with many VPCs due to the complexity and limitations in the number of peering connections that can exist between two VPCs.

Option C (Software VPN) is less scalable and more costly than Transit Gateway, as it requires maintaining multiple internet gateways and software appliances. It also uses an internet gateway for communication, which may introduce additional latency.

Option D (Direct Connect) is not suitable here because it is a dedicated connection to the AWS network and does not provide the same level of network routing flexibility or cost-effectiveness as Transit Gateway.

Option D, Software VPN, requires creating secure tunnels between two or more software appliances and uses an internet gateway for communication, which is less scalable compared to Transit Gateway (AWS-VPC-Connectivity-Options.pdf, p.37).
